palette.notes: Not hand-made pixel art: a 3D render with a low-res pixel filter, so the measured palette (0) is meaningless. Cyan water wall, jade-green door, dark moss and grey cobbles; all shadows go blue-green.

lighting: Bright cyan light from the water wall on the right and above; the left rock wall and foreground fall into dark green; the door glows mid-tone in the centre.
silhouette: No characters; a centred stone door framed by a rock wall and a waterfall is the only shape to read.

motion.timing: Measured 30 drawings/s on 1s: continuous rendered motion (water flow, shimmering caustics), not keyed pixel drawings. The view itself barely moves.

texture: Pixelated photo-like textures: noisy moss, cobbles and water streaks; no clean pixel clusters.
camera: Locked one-point perspective down a cobbled path to the door; a near-static ambient loop.

acting.acts: No characters; the scene teaches staging: one-point perspective and a lit door make the eye travel to the centre.
acting.depth: Strong depth from the converging path and walls; the door is the vanishing point where a character could appear small.

techniques: 3D render downsampled to a pixel look (not hand-placed pixels)
one-point perspective path leading to a centred door
cool cyan light side vs dark green shadow side
endless ambient loop with only water moving
feel: pixel-filtered 3D + one-point path to a lit door + only water moving = calm liminal loop (not true pixel art)
for_fred: Borrow the staging, not the look: a path leading to a door in the far background where Fred appears small, swims toward camera, then turns and goes back through. Avoid the filtered-3D texture; it fights hand-placed pixel characters.
